about: Real bugs in llama.cpp and in published GGUF files, for `infercheck bench`. Engine cases pin the llama.cpp commit before the fix (broken) and the fix (fixed); file cases pin GGUF revisions on the Hub by date; controls are GGUFs with no known bug. model.gguf and model.reference are tried in order; {"search": ...} queries the Hub. See infercheck/bench.py.

cases.title: Gemma 4's BPE vocabulary was tokenized with the SentencePiece algorithm
cases.notes: The first Gemma 4 support loaded its vocabulary as SPM; #21343 switched it to BPE with newline-only pre-splitting and raw UTF-8 bytes. The switch fixed words like " discards" but started dropping characters that need byte-fallback tokens (fixed in #21534) and crashing on some newline runs (#21406), so the fixed side has bugs of its own: only the comparison against the reference tokenizer can say which side is closer.

cases.title: Gemma 4 crashed on long inputs: its newline pre-split regex fell back to std::regex
cases.notes: The pre-tokenizer pattern [^\n]+|[\n]+ had no custom implementation, so it went through std::regex, which segfaults (stack overflow) on about 50,000 repeated characters. #21406 added a custom splitter. Checked offline with scripts/bench_offline.py: llama.cpp d0068583 segfaults on 6 of the 10 long inputs and b7ad48eb on none. The stack overflow is in libstdc++'s std::regex (GCC, so Linux); Apple's libc++ does not overflow on the same input, so the case only runs on Linux and a macOS run reports it as other-platform.

cases.title: Gemma 4's byte-fallback tokens decoded to nothing (emoji vanished from output)
cases.notes: token_to_piece had no branch for byte tokens in BPE vocabularies, so <0xF0><0x9F><0xA6><0x99> (🦙) decoded to an empty string; token_to_byte would have aborted. llama.cpp's own encoder dropped those characters at the time (fixed three days later), so an encode-and-decode round trip never produced the tokens: only decoding the reference's ids shows the bug. Checked offline with scripts/bench_offline.py: llama.cpp 941146b3 decodes ' this is 🦙.cpp' as ' this is.cpp', 4aa962e2 gets it right, and InferCheck's corpus run through both builds finds no difference.

cases.title: Gemma 4 stopped on the text token </s>
cases.notes: llama.cpp's end-of-generation auto-detection matched </s>; #21492 removes it from the EOG list (and makes it a normal token again) when the vocabulary has <|tool_response>.

cases.title: Gemma 4 silently dropped characters that need byte-fallback tokens
cases.notes: For BPE without GPT-2 byte encoding, the fallback looked up a one-byte string instead of <0xXX>, found nothing and emitted nothing.

cases.title: Gemma 4's final_logit_softcapping was not read
cases.notes: Changes the logits, not the tokenizer: InferCheck has no check for it yet (a logits comparison would).

cases.title: Tekken and GPT-4o pre-tokenizers split words at combining marks
cases.notes: Found with InferCheck (tkran2). The regex lookaheads allowed letters but not marks (\p{M}).

cases.title: GGUFs tagged "pixtral" got the Llama 3 pre-tokenizer instead of Tekken
cases.notes: Found with InferCheck (tkran2): affected NVIDIA Nemotron 3/3.5 GGUFs.

cases.title: llama.cpp removed the space before punctuation when decoding Gemma 4 and others
cases.notes: Found with InferCheck (tkran2): x != y decoded as x!= y. #30940 adds a clean_spaces GGUF key and turns the clean-up off by default for these pre-tokenizers.

cases.title: " ~" was split in two, preventing DeepSeek V4's Ġ~ merge
cases.notes: The collapsed \p{S} symbol class was missing '~'. The repos are found by search: check resolved.json.

cases.title: Qwen2-style tokenizers crashed llama.cpp on long runs of one character
cases.notes: The Qwen2 regex fell through to std::regex, whose recursive backtracking overflowed the stack (43K 'A's). InferCheck's corpus had nothing that long, so this case motivated the stress check. The stack overflow is in libstdc++'s std::regex (GCC, so Linux); Apple's libc++ does not overflow on the same input, so the case only runs on Linux and a macOS run reports it as other-platform.

cases.title: Llama 3 GGUFs converted before the BPE pre-tokenizer fix
cases.notes: Files without tokenizer.ggml.pre still load, with a warning, using the default (GPT-2) pre-tokenizer. The repo's maintainer said V1 was made before the fix. No fixed upload of the same repo, so this case counts only findings with the causes listed.

cases.title: Gemma 4 GGUFs from launch week had add_bos_token = false
cases.notes: The converter wrote add_bos_token = false, so llama.cpp gave plain-text prompts no BOS; #21500 made the converter write true and made llama.cpp override old files. This case was first scored as a wrap bug, but the run showed the original tokenizer behaves like the file before the fix: transformers adds no BOS to plain Gemma 4 text (Google's tokenizer_config.json does not set add_bos_token, and transformers 5.22.1 then adds none), and chat prompts get their BOS from the chat template in both. #21500 is llama.cpp choosing to give plain-text prompts a BOS too, which a comparison against the original tokenizer cannot call a bug, so the case is not covered.

cases.title: GLM-4-0414 GGUFs converted before the rotary-dimension fix
cases.notes: #13021 fixed three things in the GLM-4-0414 converter: the rotary dimension (half the head dimension; the old files used all of it, which gives wrong logits), the end tokens and the BOS. This case was first scored as a stop-token bug, but the run showed the end-token change made no difference: the old files took <|user|> as EOS from tokenizer_config.json and llama.cpp stops on <|endoftext|> by name, so both files stop on the same two tokens, and [gMASK] comes from the chat template either way. What users saw was the rotary dimension, which changes the logits: not covered. Both files also lack <|observation|> as a stop token; today's converter marks it (eom), so only files converted before that change are affected.

cases.title: Qwen3-Embedding GGUFs appended the wrong end token
cases.notes: The tokenizer's post-processor appends <|endoftext|>; the converter kept the config's EOS instead. Needs an upload before and after 2025-06-22; otherwise inconclusive.

cases.title: Gemma 4 GGUFs updated with Google's chat template fixes (tool calling)
cases.notes: A chat template change: InferCheck does not render templates yet, so this is expected to show nothing.

cases.title: Control: gpt-oss-20b
Control: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
Control: Qwen3 8B
cases.notes: Expected to be flagged: since llama.cpp #18825 (2026-02-20) the ordinary Qwen token "</s>" (128247) is an end-of-generation control token, so prompts containing </s> tokenize differently. Found while building this benchmark; not yet reported.

cases.title: Control: Granite 4.2 (an intentional tokenizer change)
cases.notes: Granite 4.2 tokenizes numbers and blank lines differently from 4.1 on purpose (IBM confirmed). The GGUF should match its own source model, so nothing should be flagged here.
